calls.reason: Zoom reported AI-related cost pressure but included AI without extra charges; Slack charged an add-on. These examples establish neither majority price doubling nor problematic maintenance costs, and the conclusion is hedged.

Kalai and Vempala show hallucinations arising from predictive learning even under ideal conditions; Xu and colleagues identify broader learning limits. This supports the ordinary reading of a structural tendency, without proving mitigation impossible.

Atlassian confirms bundled AI access, while Box says included usage was priced into subscriptions. Neither provides actual interaction costs or realized margins, so the packet cannot establish losses on every use.

ServiceNow describes optional customization, and Atlassian anticipates prebuilt agents. Neither supplies deployment evidence establishing mandatory programming or the limits of runtime decision-making; the broader characterization is rhetorical.

Salesforce reports growing Agentforce ARR, while TechRadar reports subdued partner adoption. Neither establishes an agent-driven growth turnaround or an expensive failure; the forecast has no deadline.

Workday and Atlassian describe workflow actions beyond conversation, but the records mix plans with existing capabilities. Without demonstrated behavior or broad coverage, they cannot settle the sweeping rebranding claim.
